summary: Patrol platform on Breezy Point, built in 1922 for use from Fishhook Peak lookout; now listed as destroyed, with cement footings still on the site.

facts.status_note: Site label reads Drive-Up Destroyed; the site writers found the cement footings.

access.note: Site label is Drive-Up; the page calls the spot a campsite and mentions no closure. Medium confidence: no agency notice was read.

visit.trail_note: Site label says Drive-Up; no trail is described.

events.note: Site page: patrol platform built here for use from Fishhook Peak Lookout. The Fishhook entry gives 1922 for the tower, not the platform.

evidence.supports: Platform built in 1922 for use from Fishhook Peak Lookout
evidence.quote: 1922: Patrol Platform built here for use from Fishhook Peak Lookout

evidence.supports: Patrol platform on Breezy Point two miles south of Fishhook Peak tower
evidence.quote: a patrol platform on Breezy Point 2 miles south

notes_for_editor: The 1922 platform date rests on one source (idahofirelookouts.com). firelookout.com corroborates the platform's existence two miles south of Fishhook Peak but gives no date for it. The brief record had status unknown; the site label now gives destroyed, with no date or cause. No photo added: the idaho_fl source record already holds the site's photo. Do not confuse with the Washington Breezy Point lookout site in the firetower.org cache (data/raw/fflos/firetower.org/lookouts/us/wa/breezy-point-lookout-site). The agency name is as the 2024 site page gives it; it was not checked against current forest records.
